title: Workload extension
description: Everything a consumer supplies to observe a workload the framework ships no content for. The whole artifact lives in a consumer-owned path, so onboarding a second workload produces no diff inside the declared core (FR-63, US-8). The extension supplies inputs and never behaviour: it carries no script, no command and no free-form payload, because an extension point that accepted code would put consumer content on the execution path and make the read-only boundary a matter of what was written rather than what is possible.

name.description: Names the workload this extends. Distinct from any framework identifier, so a consumer name can never collide with a shipped one.

targetResources.description: What this extension applies to. Non-empty: an extension targeting nothing is configuration that appears active and does nothing.

queries.description: Consumer-supplied catalogue entries. Every one is pinned to the consumerExtension origin, so an extension structurally cannot contribute an entry that claims to be a framework default. That is what keeps default and extension separable once a consumer customises.

connectorRefs.description: Names connector configurations this workload needs. Names only: an endpoint or a credential is never restated here (SEC-013).

executionLimitOverrides.description: Optional, and an empty object is rejected: a declared override that overrides nothing reads as intent that was never expressed. These narrow the limits and cannot widen them past the tool policy, which is a semantic check.

networkAccessMode.description: Declared rather than inferred, so a workload reaching a public endpoint is visible in review instead of discovered at run time.

schedule.description: When observation runs. A closed cadence rather than a free-form expression: an arbitrary schedule string is an unreviewable input, and agent-created schedules are one of the seven categories the tool policy denies outright (FR-52).

timeZone.description: An IANA zone name. That it resolves is a semantic check.

reportShaping.description: Which sections appear in the output, chosen from a closed set. Shaping selects from what the framework produces and never supplies content, so a report cannot become a channel for consumer text that was never reviewed.

schemaVersion.description: The version of this schema the instance conforms to (FR-05, FR-29).

identifier.description: Lowercase, hyphen-separated. Constrained so an identifier cannot carry arbitrary text, and English by construction (FR-03, CON-01).

sha256Hex.description: Lowercase hex, exactly 64 characters, as ADR-0004 pins.

capabilityClass.description: The same closed set the tool policy uses. An extension cannot name a class the policy does not know, so it cannot widen what the agent may do.

kind.description: Selection mechanism, deliberately not a workload type. The core ships no workload-type content of its own (FR-63, CC-022).

selector.description: A placeholder in every shipped example.

origin.description: Pinned. A single-member enumeration is what prevents an extension from supplying an entry labelled as a framework default, which would make a customised catalogue indistinguishable from a tampered one.

queryText.description: The consumer's reviewed query. Bounded above: a query too long to review is not reviewed.

queryHash.description: SHA-256 over the NFC-normalised query text, so an entry edited after review is detectable.

condition.description: The condition in the consumer's terms. Evaluated by the platform the alert is defined in, never by this framework, which observes and does not act.

queryRef.description: The catalogue entry this alert reads from. That it resolves is a semantic check.
